This page is generated from the `tools/list` response of [s1000d-brex-mcp](/s1000d-stack/mcp/brex-mcp/) 0.9.0. The s1000d-brex-mcp page explains the configuration and how to read the responses.

## Summary

Returns what an element or attribute value means in the project and which values are allowed. Pass `value` to also get whether that value is allowed

## Description returned by `tools/list`

This is the text an LLM receives.

> Explain what a value of an element or attribute means in a BREX, or list the allowed values. Pass "target" as an attribute name (e.g. "securityClassification"), an element name, or an XPath fragment; optionally "value" to check one value. Returns the matching rules with allowed values and their meanings, and whether the value is allowed.

## Arguments

The content of `inputSchema`. A nested argument is written as `parent.child`, and an item of an array as `parent[].child`.

| Name | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `brex` | `string` |  |  | Which BREX to use: a file path to a BREX data module (.xml), or a DMC (e.g. "KENBAIKI-A-00-00-00-00A-022A-D", "DMC-" prefix optional) searched in csdbDirs / S1000D_CSDB_DIR / S1000D_SPEC_DIR. Omit to use the S1000D default BREX found under S1000D_SPEC_DIR. |
| `csdbDirs` | `array<string>` |  |  | CSDB folders to search for BREX by DMC (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file; S1000D_SPEC_DIR is always searched for the S1000D default BREX). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes. |
| `target` | `string` | Yes |  | Attribute name ("infoCode", "@infoCode"), element name ("language"), or XPath fragment to match against objectPath. |
| `value` | `string` |  |  | The value to check against the allowed values (optional). |
| `context` | `string` |  |  | Schema file name (e.g. "descript") to pick context-specific rules in addition to common ones. |
